questions.prompt: Which two details matter for a useful screen?

options.text: Whether YOU can affect the goalie’s view
Whether D2 has a usable shot or pass

questions.explanation: The screen works through sightline and carrier access; standing on W crowds the net and closes support.

questions.prompt: Arrange one screen read.

options.text: Set a net-front position outside W’s route
Move if Gold 1 seals the lane

questions.explanation: The puck line shows where screening matters; separation keeps two options; a seal requires a new angle.

questions.prompt: Move YOU toward the goal line to compare a net-front position separate from W.
questions.explanation: The example changes the net-front angle and stays separate from W. Check the goalie, traffic and puck line before treating it as a screen.

questions.prompt: If Gold 1 turns to box you out, what could D2 read?

options.text: Whether the changed body position opens W or another lane
That the screen makes the goalie unable to see

questions.prompt: How can you screen without turning the play into a collision?

options.text: Locate Gold 1 near the puck line

questions.prompt: Why should D2 recheck the lane when Gold 1 follows a support move?

options.text: The original shooting lane, without checking Gold 2 or D1

questions.prompt: Arrange one second-player rebound read.

options.text: Check D1’s approach and the goalie

questions.explanation: The closest skater is not automatically the winner. Check the goalie and opponent before deciding who contests and who covers.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to a net-side cover position while D1 approaches the loose rebound.

Keep Gold 1 in the pressure scan

questions.explanation: Puck side determines route; showing a lane connects D1; Gold 1 decides whether it is safe.

questions.explanation: The example moves YOU closer to D1 while remaining across the middle. Recheck Gold 1 and D2 before calling for the pass.

options.text: Whether D2 provides the next short option or D1 protects

questions.prompt: Why does the goalie’s release change your support job?
questions.explanation: The new puck owner and side determine where a short outlet can exist, so move with the play while scanning Gold 1; if contested, support becomes protection.

sources.use: Supports age/topic placement only. The setup, alternatives and suggested answers are original experimental coaching synthesis, not source-certified.

before.limits: Static experimental practice scene. Positions are examples and do not prove timing, execution, possession outcome, or a universal team system; coaching responses are ungraded.

questions.prompt: What has Gold 1 changed?
questions.explanation: Gold 1 is stated to have moved into the direct passing connection.

questions.prompt: Which two cues should shape the next touch?

options.text: The two-on-one label decides the finish

questions.explanation: The defender, goalie and support route determine whether a shot, pass or protection is useful.

questions.prompt: Arrange a changed two-on-one read.

options.text: Compare the carrier and second option

questions.explanation: Locating Gold 1 and F2 can overlap with comparing the carrier and second option; both are part of the same scan. Re-checking the goalie and lane still comes last because the read must reflect whichever option is open right before the touch.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to compare a different angle toward F2 and the net.
questions.explanation: The example changes the carrier’s passing and shooting angles. Recheck Gold 1, F2 and the goalie before choosing; the new point does not establish an open lane.

questions.prompt: Gold 1 turns toward YOU and F2 gains separation. What could improve?

options.text: A pass if F2 remains reachable, or a shot if the goalie gives room
Ignore F2 and shoot through the defender

questions.explanation: F2 separation changes the branch, while the goalie and defender still determine whether the pass or shot is usable.

questions.prompt: How can feedback respect both a possible shot and a possible pass?
questions.explanation: Tie the choice to Gold 1, F2 and the goalie. If the defender closes the carrier but F2 is reachable, pass; if F2 is covered and the carrier lane remains open, consider the shot.

after.title: Read the second option in a two-on-one
after.objective: Update a two-on-one choice when a defender changes the passing connection.
after.briefing: Navy attacks the right net. YOU control the puck and F2 is the second attacker. Gold 1 occupies the direct line between YOU and F2. The goalie is near the net; no save or finish is established.
cues: YOU own the puck.
F2 is the second Navy attacker.
Gold 1 occupies the direct pass lane.

before.title: A defender rotates low while a forward covers the point
before.objective: Understand a declared role exchange without confusing jersey position with current responsibility.
before.briefing: F1 controls behind the Gold net. D1 has rotated low on one side. YOU are F3 and the coach has explicitly assigned YOU to cover D1’s vacated point until the exchange ends. D2 remains at the opposite point. Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. This is a selected-player teaching view; no movement is implied unless stated.
cues: The briefing explicitly assigns the vacated point during the role exchange.

F1 controls behind the Gold net. D1 has rotated low on one side. YOU are F3 and the coach has explicitly assigned YOU to cover D1’s vacated point until the exchange ends. D2 remains at the opposite point.

sources.title: Developing Skilled Defencemen — Overview
sources.section: PDF pages 20–21, Offensive Zone Play
sources.use: Supports the stated coaching principle. The setup, alternatives and suggested answers are original experimental coaching synthesis, not source-certified.

before.limits: Age adaptation and tactical alternatives await coaching review. Static setup: no skating speed, interception timing or uniquely optimal route has been validated. Positional references are examples, not scored targets.

questions.prompt: Which high area has the coach assigned YOU to cover?
questions.explanation: The briefing explicitly assigns the vacated point during the role exchange.

questions.prompt: Which two checks make that cover useful?

options.text: The opposing exit route if possession changes
The outlet from the low attack
Whether being a forward prevents high support

questions.explanation: Current responsibilities follow the stated exchange, while pressure and possession still govern position.

questions.prompt: Arrange the stated role replacement.

options.text: Check the vacated point and exit threats
Occupy useful high support and communicate

questions.explanation: This is a team-plan example, not a universal instruction for every offensive rotation.

questions.prompt: Move YOU toward the vacated point to illustrate the assigned cover.
questions.explanation: The reference replaces a high role without copying D2’s opposite point. Timing and passing lanes remain conditional.

questions.prompt: F1 loses the puck behind the net. What becomes relevant immediately?

options.text: The assigned high cover and the possible exit route
Only waiting for the planned pass
The assumption that Navy remains on offense

questions.explanation: Recheck the puck state and exit threats while moving into the assigned cover. YOU start inside the zone, so the point is not already covered in this frame.

questions.prompt: Explain the difference between your listed position as F3 and your temporary rink responsibility.
questions.explanation: A forward can fill point support under an explicit exchange; the label does not by itself determine every next action.

questions.prompt: What should YOU communicate about the temporary point cover?

options.text: I am taking the vacated point; call the low rotation
My normal position removes the assignment
D1 covers the point and low space together

questions.explanation: The message states the temporary area and asks for the teammate rotation.

questions.prompt: Which two cues affect your point responsibility?

options.text: The listed forward role decides the cover without the puck scan

questions.explanation: Carrier and teammate rotation shape the temporary responsibility.

questions.prompt: Move YOU toward the vacated point and compare the route toward F1.
questions.explanation: The example is near the attacking blue line, opposite D2 and farther from F1. Check the low outlet and exit threats; arrival and a clear pass are not established.

questions.prompt: F1 loses the puck behind the net. What do YOU communicate?
questions.explanation: Call the low threat and D1’s rotation, then keep the point connection while the new carrier and lane are identified.

before.title: Exchange the point and low roles
before.objective: Cover a temporarily assigned high area while keeping the low puck threat in view.
before.briefing: Navy attacks the right net. F1 controls behind the goal line and D1 has rotated low. YOU start inside the zone and are assigned to fill the vacated point near the blue line. Gold has five skaters shown. This is a selected-player teaching view; the assignment does not mean the point is already covered.

D1 rotates low.
Gold has low and point-side options.

questions.prompt: Which area are YOU assigned to cover for this rep?
questions.explanation: The briefing explicitly assigns YOU the high point cover for this drill.

questions.prompt: Which carrier and teammate rotation cues make the temporary cover useful?

options.text: D1's low rotation and the point lane
The normal forward role should take priority over the stated assignment

questions.explanation: The temporary job follows the carrier and the teammate rotation; usual labels do not decide the area.

questions.prompt: Arrange the role replacement.

options.text: Track the puck and point lane
Re-check D1 and the low threat

questions.explanation: The explicit assignment starts the job, then carrier and rotation guide the update.

questions.prompt: Move YOU toward the vacated point near the attacking blue line.
questions.explanation: The example moves toward the blue line, on D1’s side, and farther from F1. Check the exit threats and low outlet; reaching this point in time is not established.

questions.prompt: F1 loses it behind the net: which low threat must enter your update?

options.text: The low carrier threat and D1's rotation
Leave the point to chase any player

questions.explanation: The puck location changes the immediate threat; keep the point relationship while coordinating the low response.

questions.prompt: Explain the difference between your listed position as a forward and your temporary rink responsibility.
questions.explanation: Your label describes your normal role; the coach has assigned the point for this rep. Communicate the temporary area and update when the puck or rotation changes.
